name: LLM Maybe LongLM: Self-Extend LLM Context Window Without Tuning
problem: LLMs do not generalise to contexts longer than their training length, and the usual fixes all require fine-tuning, which is expensive and needs data the model owner may not have.
mechanism: Build BI-LEVEL attention information at inference, with no weight changes. GROUPED attention pools distant tokens into groups (and selects the most relevant groups per query) to capture long-range dependency without O(n^2); NEIGHBOR attention handles nearby tokens within a specified local range with the original exact self-attention. Both are computed from the existing model's own attention mechanism with a small code modification, so the weights are untouched.
speedup_reported: NOT RECORDED AS A NUMBER. The abstract's claim is qualitative and capability-shaped: SelfExtend effectively extends existing LLMs' context window length, evaluated across multiple benchmarks, with 'minor code modification' and no fine-tuning. No multiple, no baseline, no hardware. The deployment-relevant property is architectural: no retraining and no architecture change means it applies to an already-trained checkpoint.

The efficient ecosystem instead adopted the RoPE-rescaling family of context extension - yarn, longrope, position-interpolation, all recorded separately here and all in-upstream-engine - because a rescaling config is consumed by existing kernels whereas grouped+neighbor attention needs new attention code per head. That contrast is the useful lesson in this record. The grouping mechanism does resemble what H2O/Quest do, but at prefill rather than at KV eviction.
